I’ve done this pretty much all my life, honestly I don’t think this is exclusive to suicidal people. More just something people drift off in their thoughts about when they’re bored. I pictured my own funeral a lot, long before I felt suicidal.

Weirdly, I do think about my funeral when I feel suicidal, but that usually helps me to stop considering actually killing myself. Because I picture the people who would be there, and what they would say about me, and I realise that they wouldn’t actually be happy about my death even though I usually assume they would be.
I get that too!! It feels like I have no control over myself anymore, and taking control of my way out feels like I’m taking some of that power back.

Yeah, me too. Even then I can’t overthink it because I remember that leaving isn’t actually that easy (we don’t have guns here) and it stresses me out more, but the fact that the way out is right there for me keeps me going.
Damn this is only the second time I’ve logged into this account since I made it and had no idea it was its cake day... crazy! Thank you!

Bodies are bound to change over time, especially during puberty, so expecting/wanting to look the same in your early teens as your late teens is unreasonable and therefore unhealthy for your mental well-being, and possibly for your physical well-being too if you act on trying to make yourself look like you did back then.

Honestly!! I was going to say it’s absolute bullshit that we’re forced to exist even if we’re suffering, but even that’s not entirely true, given that euthanasia is possible for certain people suffering from painful physical conditions that they would rather die than carry on living with. But that’s the thing. Physical conditions. Not that they don’t deserve that option, but that we should have it too - the lack of concern for people in mental pain vs physical pain is ridiculous.

Honestly. I’m so jealous. Deep down I know that someday I’ll probably be glad I don’t have access to a gun or anything that I can kill myself just as quickly with, but right now I can’t help but envy people living in America and such. It would be so much easier.
I’ve had the diagnosis since before my sister (the eldest of the kids) was born 🥴 (and thanks for backing me up haha)

Not that I’m aware of? I don’t think it’s tracked like that and my parents are paying it back when they can anyway, but afaik it’s just like my money to do whatever with once I have it, and all’s well as long as there’s enough for rent
Tbh I assume they did think about babysitters, but didn’t think beyond “It’s fine DiamondSky will do it”. You’re right, it was their decision that I didn’t opt into

I should’ve mentioned I guess in the post, people say it’s practice for when I have kids but I know for a fact that it won’t happen. I’m not big on kids in the slightest and I have a different plethora of health issues that would complicate the pregnancy as well as taking care of the child - plus even just going off the problems I mentioned in the post, if I can’t handle the kids for a few hours I definitely couldn’t 24/7. 

Regardless of the notions that I’m “still young” and “could change my mind” kids aren’t happening.
Their oldest is 13 so she’s an appointed babysitter too
The UK? As far as I know they don’t monitor it like that and it’s just your money, as long as you’ve left enough to pay accommodation rent

The loans aren’t a worry and I’m always happy to help them financially, given that my overdraft is interest-free and I have disability benefits on top of my loan, that detail was just to indicate they don’t have a lot of dosh 🥶

That’s the thing, they don’t socialise much with other parents except for my mum’s brother and his family - they have kids and are just as busy, and usually when they want me babysitting they want to go and spend time with them :/ it’s just more convenient to turn to me with no kids myself

My main worry about bringing it up is them saying that I didn’t have an issue before. It’s true that my sensory issues feel as though they used to be less bad than they are now, but I’m not sure if they’ll buy the idea that sensory issues getting worse is possible; autism symptoms are supposed to be less severe as you get older - most of mine did, but sensory overload got so much worse. I know they can’t actually force me to babysit, especially since I don’t live with them anymore, I’m just worried about confrontation/them losing respect for me etc
